explanation: Foods consist of energy-rich molecules, primarily carbohydrates, fats, and proteins. Metabolic reactions are divided into catabolism (degradative, exergonic reactions that release energy) and anabolism (synthetic, endergonic reactions that consume energy). During catabolism, glucose is broken down in glycolysis and respiration; fats are cleaved into glycerol and three fatty acids; and proteins are broken down into amino acids. Amino acids undergo deamination (removal of the amino group, -NH2) in the liver. Deamination yields toxic ammonia (NH3), which the liver quickly converts into less harmful urea. The remaining carbon chains, whose processing varies by R-group, enter the respiratory pathways at various stages.

opts: Synthetic reactions that are endergonic (consume energy)
Degradative reactions that are exergonic (release energy)
An alternative pathway for nitrogen fixation
The active transport of ions against their gradient

opts: Nitrous oxide, converted to nitrogen gas
